newsitem.title: USA: Intel sees higher fourth quarter revenues.
newsitem.headline: Intel sees higher fourth quarter revenues.

text.p: Intel Corp., the world's largest maker of semiconductors, Wednesday said it expected higher revenues in the fourth quarter, reflecting strong holiday season sales for personal computers.

The maker of popular Pentium and Pentium Pro computer microprocessors said in a statement it expected fourth quarter sales to be "significantly higher" than the $5.14 billion generated in the third quarter ended Sept. 30.

Intel's forecast came one day after California voters defeated a ballot initiative that would have expanded federal securities laws by giving investors the right to sue companies and executives in state court. Last month, Intel suspended making forward-looking statements due to the proposed law.

Bellwether technology company Intel expects its fourth quarter gross margin to rise above the third quarter's 57 percent, which is around 5 percent higher than their traditional goal. In 1995's fourth quarter, Intel generated about $4.58 billion in revenue, and its gross margin was around 48 percent.
Intel expects fourth quarter expenses to rise about 17 percent to 20 percent from the third quarter's $1.01 billion due to higher holiday advertising costs and co-marketing programmes.
The company reduced its capital expenditure forecast for all of 1996 to less than $3.4 billion from a previous $3.6 billion due to delays in buidling new administration offices.
